description: Provider-neutral contract for the Android client CI/release pipelines. GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/build-by-pull-request.yml, release-by-dev.yml, release-by-main.yml, release-by-tag.yml) and Azure DevOps (azure-pipelines.yml, azure-release.yml) are thin adapters around the shared scripts under scripts/ci/. scripts/ci/check_pipeline_parity.py fails when either adapter drifts from this file. Change this file first, then the adapters.

toolchain.androidSdkNote: platforms;android-37 is deliberately NOT installed here: the runner bundled sdkmanager cannot resolve it and Gradle/AGP auto-downloads it mid-build (docs/guides/troubleshooting.md).

signing.note: Only release pipelines materialize the keystore. The PR pipelines never receive signing secrets; the PR release build is an unsigned sanity build.

changeDetection.note: media is a submodule: its pointer bump is reported as the bare path 'media'.
changeDetection.replayBaseline: latest release tag (-auto(N)) reachable from the replay commit; an empty range skips
changeDetection.azureBeforeSource: azure has no push 'before' sha: the previous completed build of the same pipeline and branch is used, then the replay baseline

buildNumber.rule: highest N among tags ending in -auto(N), plus 1; shared by mobile and tv version codes
buildNumber.serialization: one release at a time across dev, main and tag flows

status.postedBy: the provider that actually ran CI

github-android-pr-ci-pat.purpose: Azure PR CI build job only: guard (Variables read) and private submodule checkout (Contents read). READ-ONLY: no commit statuses, no Contents write, no Actions write, no Variables write; PR-controlled code runs with it.

github-android-pr-gate-pat.purpose: Azure PR CI gate job only: posts the CI Gate commit status (Commit statuses write, nothing else). Loaded and used only by trusted target-branch scripts, never by a job that runs PR-controlled code.

github-android-release-pat.purpose: Azure release only: private submodules, tags and GitHub Releases (Contents read+write), provider guard and stale-replay check (Variables read).

android-signing-keystore-base64.purpose: Release keystore (single-line base64, identical to the GitHub secret value).

github-android-provider-switch-pat.purpose: Provider switch: Actions read+write (replay dispatch) and repository Variables read+write. Loaded only by the trusted monthly reset workflow (OIDC on main) or an operator; never by a pull-request-triggered pipeline.

azure-devops-android-pipeline-control-pa.purpose: Azure DevOps PAT (Build read and execute) that enables/disables both Azure pipelines and queues the destination replay.

additionalWorkflows..github/workflows/ci-provider-reset.yml: GitHub-only by design: the monthly reset runs on a GitHub schedule and restores github as the provider.
additionalWorkflows.audit: No other workflow builds, signs, publishes or recovers an Android release; the four workflows above are the complete set.

intentionalDifferences.detail: GitHub posts the PR comment with artifact links. Azure does not: the Azure PR tokens are read-only or statuses-only (least privilege), so the artifact link travels in the CI Gate status target_url instead.

GitHub posts the CI Gate status from a checkout-free github-script job (job-level statuses: write only there) using the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN; Azure posts it from a separate gate job with its own identity and a statuses-only token, running android_ci.py and the vault loader from a copy of the target branch (first parent of the PR merge commit), never from the PR tree. Same context, same states; Azure posts no pending status.

GitHub's PR build checks out with the read-only secret PR_CI_READ_PAT and persist-credentials false; the release PAT GH_PAT is never referenced by the PR workflow. Azure's build job holds the read-only Key Vault secret github-android-pr-ci-pat.
GitHub caches Gradle through setup-java/setup-gradle; Azure builds without a Gradle cache (correctness is unaffected, builds are slower).

GitHub dev release uses an on.push.paths filter; Azure cannot scope a path filter to one branch of a shared trigger, so the dev/main run always starts and change detection (the same code-path regex) skips it before any build work.
JDK, Gradle cache and Android command-line tool installers are provider-native actions/tasks; the versions and package lists they install come from this contract.

GitHub keeps using GitHub Actions secrets. Azure reads the same values from Key Vault through per-pipeline identities. The Key Vault values are populated once by an operator; nothing is copied into Azure pipeline variables.
Retention days are a GitHub setting; Azure uses the organization retention policy.
GitHub uses the push before-sha; Azure has none and uses the previous completed build of the same branch, falling back to the latest release tag.

GitHub serializes with concurrency group release-build-number (cancel-in-progress false); Azure uses lockBehavior sequential plus an Exclusive Lock check on the android-release-build-number environment. The two providers never run at once: the switch refuses while the provider being left has a release in flight.
GitHub has one workflow per release type; Azure has one pipeline (azure-release.yml) that selects the release type from the triggering ref (android_ci.py resolve-mode).

Release publication (tag, GitHub Release, Versions API) moved from inline steps and ncipollo/release-action into android_ci.py so both providers run identical code. dev, main and tag releases now share the beta Gradle profile (--no-daemon, 6g heap).
